raw_case_text: A 45-year-old Chinese woman presented with half a month history of cough and expectoration to our hospital in May 2019. Physical examinations were unremarkable. No obvious abnormalities were found in laboratory tests, including blood routine, serum biochemistry and tumor biomarkers. A computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest on May 25 revealed a high-density shadow in inferior lobe of right lung (Figure 1A). The enhanced CT was performed after 2 weeks' treatment with oral moxifloxacin on June 7, which revealed a little progress of the lesion (Figure 1B). The patient underwent bronchoscopy and aspergillus fumigatus was detected in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Therefore, the patient was treated with oral voriconazole (200mg q12h) for more than 1 months. However, the patient's symptoms worsened. The re-checked CT on July 27 demonstrated marked progression of the lesion in inferior lobe of right lung (Figure 1C) and a new lesion of ground grass opacity (GGO) was also found in the lower left lobe (Figure 1D). Then, voriconazole treatment was discontinued and the patient underwent CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy and pathological results showed lung adenocarcinoma (Figure 2). The tumor tissue was subjected to next-generation sequencing (NGS), using a commercial gene panel targeting 168 cancer-related genes (Burning Rock Biotech Ltd, Guangzhou, China). The NGS reports revealed the KIF5B-EGFR, a novel rearrangement of the EGFR gene that has not been reported previously (Figure 3). The patient began treatment with afatinib (40mg qd po) and bevacizumab (400mg q3w ivgtt) since August 14. She experienced sustained clinical improvement after anti-tumor therapy and a CT scan on October 13 revealed marked decrease of the infiltrations on the lower right lung (Figure 1E) and the absence of GGO on the left lung, assessed as partial remission. The patient had mild rash and diarrhea during treatment, which was considered an adverse reaction associated with EGFR-TKI. Encouragingly, the lesion on the right lower lung continued to shrink during the treatment (Figure 1F-H). Thus far, the patient feels well and the disease has remained stable. She has been continuing treatment with afatinib and bevacizumab and will be followed up regularly.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 45-year-old Chinese woman presented with a 2-week history of cough and expectoration that worsened over the subsequent 2 months despite oral moxifloxacin and voriconazole therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In May 2019, the patient presented with a half-month history of cough and expectoration and a right lower lobe consolidation on chest CT. After 2 weeks of oral moxifloxacin showed slight radiographic progression, bronchoscopy detected Aspergillus fumigatus in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, and she was treated with oral voriconazole (200 mg every 12 hours) for >1 month. However, her respiratory symptoms worsened and repeat chest CT on July 27, 2019 showed marked progression of the right lower lobe lesion and a new left lower lobe ground-glass opacity.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for persistent worsening cough and expectoration; later developed mild treatment-related rash and diarrhea on afatinib.

objective.routine_investigations: Routine complete blood count, serum biochemistry, and serum tumor biomarkers were within normal limits.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial chest CT (May 25, 2019) showed a high-density shadow in the right lower lobe that progressed slightly on June 7 after moxifloxacin and progressed markedly with a new left lower lobe ground-glass opacity on July 27 despite >1 month of oral voriconazole. Initial bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) detected Aspergillus fumigatus. Subsequent CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy of the progressing right lower lobe mass established primary lung adenocarcinoma, and 168-gene targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) identified a novel KIF5B-EGFR kinase domain fusion rearrangement.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Primary right lower lobe lung adenocarcinoma harboring a novel KIF5B-EGFR fusion rearrangement initially masked by secondary airway colonization/co-detection of Aspergillus fumigatus in BAL fluid (evidenced by marked tumor progression despite >1 month of oral voriconazole 200 mg q12h and definitive CT-guided lung biopsy pathology and NGS). Voriconazole was discontinued, and targeted therapy with oral afatinib (40 mg daily) combined with intravenous bevacizumab (400 mg every 3 weeks) initiated on August 14, 2019 achieved sustained clinical improvement, complete resolution of the left lung ground-glass opacity, and a durable partial response of the right lower lobe mass.
